front: What is a **book of prime entry**?
back: A book in which transactions are first recorded, in date order and by type, before posting to the ledger.

front: Which book records a credit note issued to a customer?
Which book records a credit note received from a supplier?
What goes in the general journal?
back: Opening entries, non-current assets bought or sold on credit, write-offs and corrections, each with a narrative.

front: Discount columns in the cash book
back: Memorandum columns: discount allowed (receipts side) and discount received (payments side); totals posted at the end of the month.
Total: debit Trade receivables control, credit Sales. Items: debit each customer in the sales ledger.
A general ledger account summarising a subsidiary ledger; its balance equals the total of the individual balances.
Capital is the balancing figure: total assets less total liabilities.
Better control and detection of errors, information for management, customer and supplier statements; the cost is time and money.
